name: Teke-Fuumu
world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.source_named: Makouta-Mboukou, Jean-Pierre 1977. Etude descriptive du fumu, dialecte teke de Ngamaba, Brazzaville (long grammar). Not online.

new_statements.quote: L'usage seul peut apprendre la place de l'accent tonique. Tout ce qu'on peut dire c'est que : 1° les mots de deux syllabes ont ordinairement l'accent sur la première ; 2° les mots de trois et quatre syllabes ont ordinairement l'accent sur la seconde. Cependant beaucoup de mots de trois syllabes ont l'accent sur la première ; 3° les verbes ont ordinairement l'accent sur la première. Remarques. — 1° Les préfixes comptent comme syllabes dans les noms. 2° Les pronoms conjoints ne comptent pas dans les verbes. 3° Les particules ne comptent pas dans les adjectifs.
new_statements.translation: Only usage can teach the place of the tonic accent. All one can say is that: 1° words of two syllables ordinarily have the accent on the first; 2° words of three and four syllables ordinarily have the accent on the second. However, many three-syllable words have the accent on the first; 3° verbs ordinarily have the accent on the first. Remarks. — 1° Prefixes count as syllables in nouns. 2° Conjoint (subject) pronouns do not count in verbs. 3° Particles do not count in adjectives.
new_statements.citation: Calloc'h, J. (1911). Vocabulaire français-ifumu (batéké) précédé d'éléments de grammaire. Préface de A. Meillet. Paris: Librairie Paul Geuthner.
new_statements.locator: Éléments de grammaire (Essai de grammaire ifumu), Préliminaire, p. 5, section 'L'accent tonique' (PDF page 17 of the saved Internet Archive scan)
new_statements.rule_in_words: Accent position is not fully predictable ('usage alone can teach it'); tendencies: initial in disyllables, second syllable in three- and four-syllable words (with many trisyllables initial), initial in verbs; the noun class prefix counts as a syllable, verb subject clitics and adjectival particles do not. The same page states the accent is distinct from vowel length and that syllables following an accented or long syllable are barely audible. Caution: a 1911 missionary 'accent tonique' in a tonal Teke language very likely reflects (high) tone rather than stress; the disyllable-initial / longer-word-second tendency is consistent with a tonal reading.
new_statements.exceptions: Many trisyllables accented on the first instead of the second (p. 5); the verb bula carries a fixed 'accent euphonétique' on -la, contrary to all other verbs and to the accent/elision rules (p. 7); homonyms are distinguished by prefix, tonic accent, or length, e.g. mbali 'demain' vs mbáli 'plaies' (pp. 65-66); comparative forms luru/bvulu for luri/bvuli attributed to 'un effet d'accent tonique' (p. 73).
new_statements.domain_note: Word level (nouns with class prefix counted; verb stems without subject clitics; adjectives without particles). Whether 'accent tonique' is stress or tone is not disambiguated by the source; it distinguishes it only from length ('accent temporel'). Describes Ifumu of the Batéké of French Congo between Brazzaville and the Alima (Fumu proper).
new_statements.identity_note: Calloc'h 1911 describes 'Ifumu', which he presents as one of the three principal dialects of the Batéké of French Congo (with Isi-hàna and Itéo/Itio), spoken between Brazzaville and the Alima and 'a middle ground' between the other two; this is Fumu proper = Teke-Fuumu, glottocode teke1274 (Bantu B77b, ISO ifm). Makouta-Mboukou 1977 covers the Fumu of Ngamaba (Brazzaville), same variety. Matakumba 1982 is labelled B78, i.e. probably the Wuumu dialect that Glottolog folds into teke1274.

sources.note: Éléments de grammaire, Préliminaire p. 5 'L'accent tonique': accent plays the greatest role for intelligibility; distinct from vowel length; post-tonic syllables barely audible; placement learnable only by usage, but ordinarily initial in disyllables, on the 2nd syllable in 3-4-syllable words (many trisyllables initial), initial in verbs; noun prefixes count as syllables, verb subject clitics and adjective particles do not. p. 7: verb bula has an 'accent euphonétique' on -la, always accented. pp. 65-66: homonyms distinguished by prefix, tonic accent or length (mbali 'demain' vs mbáli 'plaies'…
Nothing on stress; lists Pacchiarotti, Chousou-Polydouri & Bostoen 2019 (subclassification) and Ethnologue 2025 as references; descriptive refs are the three above.
Nothing on phonology; only that Fuumu, Wuumu and Mpuono are dialects of a Teke continuum.
